n: A festival song: sing loudly to God our strength; shout for joy to the God of Jacob.
Strike up the music — tambourine, sweet harp and lyre.

f.g: A stringed instrument like a lyre.

n: Blow the ram’s horn at the new moon and the full moon, on the feast day. This likely refers to the Feast of Trumpets and Tabernacles in the autumn.

f.g: At the full moon — when the great festivals began.

n: These festivals were commanded by God as part of Israel’s law.
God established this as a witness when he went out against Egypt. Then a new voice speaks: “I heard a language I didn’t know” — the psalmist receiving a prophetic word.

f.w: I heard a language that I understood not
f.g: Perhaps an unfamiliar voice — God’s — speaking an unexpected message.

n: Now God speaks: I lifted the heavy load from Israel’s shoulders and freed their hands from carrying baskets of clay in Egypt.

f.w: I removed his shoulder from the burden

f.g: Baskets used to carry bricks or clay.

n: You called in trouble and I rescued you. I answered you from the hidden thundercloud at Sinai, and tested you at the waters of Meribah.
Listen, my people, while I warn you — if only you would listen!
You shall have no foreign god among you or bow to any foreign god. This echoes the first commandment.

f.w: There shall no strange god be in thee

n: I am the Lord who brought you out of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it — God longs to give generously.

f.w: I am the LORD thy God
open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it

n: But my people wouldn’t listen; Israel wanted nothing to do with me.
So I let them follow their stubborn hearts and their own plans. Sometimes God’s judgment is simply letting people have their way.

f.w: I gave them up unto their own hearts' lust

n: A heartbreaking cry from God himself: “Oh, if only my people would listen and walk in my ways!”

f.w: Oh that my people had hearkened unto me

n: I would quickly have defeated their enemies.
Those who hate the Lord would cringe before him, and Israel’s blessing would last forever.

f.g: Israel’s time of prosperity — or the enemies’ time of punishment.

n: God would have fed them with the finest wheat and satisfied them with honey from the rock. The psalm ends with what could be — an open invitation still waiting.
